candidates.name: llm-cascade-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # f: Features of the current partial seed set (seeds already chosen this round count as active):
    #    f.a (M, n) active in-neighbours, f.E (M, n) exposure, f.eligible (M, n) bool
    #    (inactive and not chosen), f.indeg (n,), f.community (n,)
    # state.status (M, n) in {0 inactive, 1 active, 2 removed}; region_mask (n,) bool;
    # chosen (M, n) bool seeds already picked this round.
    # graph.adj / graph.adjT: see spec; prob(a): (M, n) hypothetical activation probs.
    # Return the (M, n) gain of adding each node as the next seed.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)              # hub's one-round marginal per target
    Pu = np.where(f.eligible, np.clip(P1, 0.0, 1.0), 0.0)
    A = graph.adjT
    # hub term: spread to out-neighbours + the seed itself (non-zero reach keeps ties sane)
    gain = D @ A + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # second wave: a newly activated out-neighbour u stays active for one round and
    # drives its own out-neighbours next round -- hub never counts this value.
    S1 = D @ A                                          # expected activations u would drive
    wave2 = (Pu * S1) @ A
    return gain + wave2

candidates.name: llm-wear-net
candidates.source:
NAME = "wear-net"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Same spec; targets hypotheses with exposure wear-out (e.g. H0), where an
    # extra exposure round on a node that fails to activate multiplies its future
    # probability by delta. hub spends exposure as if it were free.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    A = graph.adjT
    # Estimate the per-exposure wear factor without hard-coding delta: for a node
    # already past its activation threshold (prob decreasing in a), the ratio
    # prob(a+1)/prob(a) is exactly the wear multiplier.
    sat = f.eligible & (P1 < P0 - 1e-12) & (P0 > 1e-9)
    if sat.any():
        d = float(np.clip(np.median(P1[sat] / P0[sat]), 0.05, 1.0))
    else:
        d = 1.0
    # Standing potential of u over the next couple of rounds (best prob reachable soon).
    pfut = np.minimum(np.minimum(prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)), prob(f.a + 2))
    # Expected future value destroyed by exposing u without activating it.
    pen = (1.0 - d) * np.clip(1.0 - P1, 0.0, 1.0) * pfut
    net = np.where(f.eligible, D - pen, 0.0)
    return net @ A + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)            # keeps hub's non-zero reach term

candidates.name: llm-cascade-3
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-3"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Same spec; depth-3 expected-reward reach with wear-out discounting, because
    # the reward counts activations in every round while hub values only one hop.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    Pu = np.where(f.eligible, np.clip(P1, 0.0, 1.0), 0.0)
    A = graph.adjT
    gain = D @ A + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)              # hub's one-step term
    S1 = D @ A                                          # what an activated u drives next round
    w2 = (Pu * S1) @ A                                  # wave 2 (undiscounted, one hop away)
    # Estimate the per-exposure wear factor: on saturated nodes prob(a+1)/prob(a)=delta.
    sat = f.eligible & (P1 < P0 - 1e-12) & (P0 > 1e-9)
    if sat.any():
        d = float(np.clip(np.median(P1[sat] / P0[sat]), 0.05, 1.0))
    else:
        d = 1.0
    S2 = d * w2                                         # u's two-step drive, one extra wear round
    w3 = (Pu * S2) @ A                                  # wave 3
    return gain + w2 + w3

candidates.name: llm-cascade-lookahead
candidates.source:
NAME = "cascade-lookahead"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Hub-style immediate value ...
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    base = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # ... plus a one-round lookahead: the nodes this seed activates now become
    # active in-neighbours next round and push the cascade further.  This is
    # what hub ignores: hub only prices the spread *this* round, not the second
    # wave that the newly activated nodes will drive in the next round.
    V = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + D          # expected activations caused by seeding u
    Y = V @ graph.adjT                       # expected extra active in-neighbours next round
    a_next = np.clip(f.a + Y, 0.0, None)
    P_next = prob(a_next)
    gain_next = np.clip(P_next - P0, 0.0, None)
    return base + 0.8 * gain_next * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-fresh-target
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-target"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # Exposure wear-out: a target that has already been exposed in past rounds
    # yields progressively less payoff from additional exposures.  Hub spends
    # spread on worn-out nodes as if it were as valuable as on fresh ones.
    past = np.clip(f.E - f.a, 0.0, 30.0)
    w = 1.0 / (1.0 + 0.5 * past)             # discount spread into worn regions
    spread = (D * w) @ graph.adjT
    seed_self = f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # Prefer seeding fresh nodes with a real own-activation chance: their one
    # round of exposure is not being wasted against the wear-out decay.
    seed_self = seed_self * (1.0 + 0.3 * (past < 0.5).astype(float))
    return spread + seed_self + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-gate-spreader
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-spreader"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    hub = D @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)
    # Nodes one active in-neighbour away from tipping under the current law
    # (detected through prob, not hard-coded thresholds).
    comp = f.eligible & (f.a >= 1) & (P1 >= 0.25) & (P0 <= 0.5 * P1)
    # Value a seed by how many near-gates it would reach next round if it fires:
    # gate-2 only counts gates reachable from the seed itself; this also rewards
    # pure spreaders sitting adjacent to clusters of near-gates, which gate-2
    # ignores and hub prices too weakly.
    gate_reach = (comp * P1) @ graph.adjT
    return hub + 0.6 * gate_reach + 1e-3 * f.eligible

candidates.name: llm-chain-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "chain-2"   # two-step cascade: a seed that completes a gate also seeds the next round

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)      # prob target activates given this seed
    spread1 = D @ graph.adjT                     # direct value: marginal activations among out-neighbours
    # if v activates from u's seed, next round v is a driver: worth sum of its out-neighbours' marginals
    chain = (D * spread1) @ graph.adjT
    gain = spread1 + 0.5 * chain + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) + 1e-3 * f.eligible
    return gain

candidates.name: llm-fresh-hub
candidates.source:
NAME = "fresh-hub"   # hub, but spreading is priced by target freshness (fatigue-aware)

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    # quadratic penalty proxy for exposure fatigue: over-exposed out-neighbours are poor targets
    fresh = 1.0 / (1.0 + np.maximum(f.E - 2.0, 0.0) ** 2)
    gain = (D * fresh) @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0) * fresh + 1e-3 * f.eligible
    return gain

candidates.name: llm-gate-plus
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-plus"   # gate structure, but weights taken from prob instead of hard constants

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    near = np.where(f.eligible, P1, 0.0)         # how valuable is one more active in-neighbour here?
    comp = (f.a >= 1).astype(float) * near       # completing a gate, weighted by true activation prob
    prog = (f.a < 1).astype(float) * near        # pushing toward the gate, discounted the same way
    gain = (comp + 0.3 * prog) @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * f.eligible
    return gain

candidates.name: llm-gate-viable
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-viable"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # gate-2 wastes 0.3-weight progress credit on nodes that can never activate
    # under node-gate laws (H1: indeg >= 2). Calling prob with a large a-count
    # isolates the a-independent node gate, so we can drop dead targets.
    viable = (prob(f.a + 10.0) > 1e-9) & f.eligible
    comp = viable & (f.a == 1)
    prog = viable & (f.a < 1)
    return (comp + 0.3 * prog).astype(float) @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * viable

candidates.name: llm-gate-hub-mix
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-hub-mix"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Blend gate urgency with hub's marginal spread and self-activation term.
    # Under the soft logistic (H0) nodes still below threshold have nonzero
    # activation mass, so pure comp/prog scoring leaves that value on the table.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    D = np.where(f.eligible, P1 - P0, 0.0)
    comp = f.eligible & (f.a == 1)
    prog = f.eligible & (f.a < 1)
    base = (comp + 0.3 * prog).astype(float) + 0.5 * D
    return base @ graph.adjT + f.eligible * (1.0 - P0)

candidates.name: llm-gate-chain-2
candidates.source:
NAME = "gate-chain-2"

def objective(f, state, region_mask, chosen, graph, prob):
    # Two-step lookahead: completing a gate target is worth more if that target
    # itself has out-neighbours close to their own threshold, because its
    # activation feeds the next round. gate-2 is blind to this downstream chain.
    P0, P1 = prob(f.a), prob(f.a + 1)
    comp = f.eligible & (f.a == 1)
    prog = f.eligible & (f.a < 1)
    unlocked = (P1 - P0) @ graph.adjT          # value created at out-neighbours
    w = (comp + 0.3 * prog).astype(float) + 0.3 * comp * unlocked
    return w @ graph.adjT + 1e-3 * f.eligible
